# odoo-work-cli mcp

## NAME

odoo-work-cli-mcp - Run the MCP server on stdin/stdout (started by the MCP client)

## SYNOPSIS

```text
odoo-work-cli mcp [--read-only]
odoo-work-cli mcp COMMAND [OPTIONS]
```

## DESCRIPTION

Run a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server on standard input and output.

The MCP client (Claude Code, an IDE, any agent host) starts it as a child
process and talks newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 with it: initialize, ping,
tools/list and tools/call. There is no port and no daemon. Protocol revisions
2025-11-25, 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26 and 2024-11-05 are supported.

Every tool is one command of this CLI. A call runs that command in-process
with --json, so validation, output fields and error kinds are exactly those of
the CLI. Read tools: whoami, projects, tasks, entries, timesheets,
clock_status, clock_list. Write tools: entries_add, entries_update,
entries_delete, clock_in, clock_out, clock_add, clock_edit. The tools carry
the MCP annotations readOnlyHint, destructiveHint and idempotentHint;
entries_update, entries_delete and clock_edit are destructive.

A failed call is not a protocol error: it is a tool result with isError set
and the JSON error envelope {"error":{"kind":"…","message":"…"}}. Results
larger than 32 KiB come in pages; the second content item carries the cursor
of the next page.

Configuration and secrets load on the first tool call that needs them, not at
start: the server starts and lists its tools even with 1Password locked, and
such a call reports secrets_locked. The next call tries again; once loaded, the
connection is kept for the life of the server. The global flags --config and
--backend given before mcp apply to every call.

Nothing is written to standard output except protocol messages; standard
error stays empty.

Subcommands:

[`odoo-work-cli mcp print`](odoo-work-cli-mcp-print.md)
:   Print the MCP client configuration for this server.

## OPTIONS

`--read-only`
:   Serve only the read tools (no entries_add, entries_update, entries_delete, clock_in, clock_out, clock_add, clock_edit).

    *flag; optional*

## GLOBAL OPTIONS

`--backend` *BACKEND*
:   BACKEND: odoo or fake (offline, made-up data; env ODOO_WORK_CLI_BACKEND).

    *string; optional; default: odoo; env: ODOO_WORK_CLI_BACKEND*

`--config` *FILE*
:   Read only the config FILE (skip discovery).

    *string; optional*

`-h`, `--help`
:   Print the help of the command and exit.

## OUTPUT

Only MCP protocol messages, one JSON-RPC 2.0 response per line on standard output. A tool result's first content item is the --json output of the command; see the MCP tool reference.

## ENVIRONMENT

`ODOO_URL`
:   Odoo server URL; overrides url from the config files.

`ODOO_DATABASE`
:   Odoo database name; overrides database.

`ODOO_USERNAME`
:   Odoo login, usually an e-mail address; overrides username.

`ODOO_PASSWORD`
:   Odoo API key, used for XML-RPC. Despite the name, not the login password.

`ODOO_WEB_PASSWORD`
:   Odoo login password, used for the web session of clock in and clock out.

`ODOO_TOTP_SECRET`
:   TOTP secret (base32 or otpauth:// URL) for accounts with two-factor authentication.

`ODOO_OP_TIMEOUT`
:   Timeout of the 1Password call that resolves [op_secrets], a Go duration; default 5s.

`ODOO_WORK_CLI_NO_OP`
:   If 1, true, yes or on, [op_secrets] is ignored and the 1Password CLI is never called.

`ODOO_WORK_CLI_BACKEND`
:   Backend, odoo (default) or fake; --backend overrides it.

`ODOO_WORK_CLI_FAKE_STATE`
:   State file of the fake backend; default odoo-work-cli-fake-state.json in the temporary directory.

`XDG_CONFIG_HOME`
:   Base directory of the global config file; default ~/.config.

## FILES

`~/.config/odoo-work-cli/config.toml`
:   Global configuration ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME/odoo-work-cli/config.toml if XDG_CONFIG_HOME is set). Created by odoo-work-cli config install.

`.odoo-work-cli.toml`
:   Configuration of a directory tree. Every such file from the filesystem root down to the current directory is merged over the global file, the deepest last. --config FILE loads only FILE instead.

`$TMPDIR/odoo-work-cli-fake-state.json`
:   State of the fake backend (--backend fake); ODOO_WORK_CLI_FAKE_STATE sets another path. Delete it to start over with the seed data.

## EXIT STATUS

0 on success, 1 on any error, including usage errors. The error is printed as "Error: TEXT" on standard error.

Error kinds this command can fail with:

`auth`
:   Authentication failed: wrong API key or login password, TOTP rejected.

`validation`
:   Invalid input: unknown flag, bad argument, malformed date, time or hours, a time in the future, an unknown project.

`network`
:   Odoo cannot be reached: DNS, connection refused, timeout, TLS.

`config`
:   The local configuration is missing or invalid.

`secrets_locked`
:   1Password is locked or unreachable, so op:// references could not be resolved.

`internal`
:   Anything else: an unexpected Odoo response or a bug.

## EXAMPLES

Register the server for Claude Code (user scope):

```console
$ claude mcp add --scope user odoo-work-cli -- odoo-work-cli mcp
```

Only the read tools, against the offline fake backend:

```console
$ odoo-work-cli --backend fake mcp --read-only
```

One request by hand:

```console
$ echo '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list"}' | odoo-work-cli mcp
```
